title: Point orient at the playbook file the project really has
action: D1. orient.rs builds the class packet with playbook = skills/bee-planning/playbooks/<class>.md (line ~741) and render_class_text prints situation lines with the same fixed root (line ~757). Add one resolver that, given the project root, returns the first existing bee-planning skill directory among skills/bee-planning, .claude/skills/bee-planning, .agents/skills/bee-planning, .opencode/skills/bee-planning, and use it for the packet playbook path and every situation path, so --json and text agree; store each situation's resolved path in the packet. When none exists, the playbook and situation values name the skill instead: 'skill bee-planning: playbooks/<class>/<name>.md — load bee-planning with skill_get and open this file under its local.path'. render_class_text ends with exactly one line starting 'next: ' that tells the agent to pick the situation whose trigger phrases match the task, open that file, and make the todo list from its numbered steps (when the class has no situation lines: open the playbook file). Update orient's --help text if it names the fixed path and run bee dev regen so registry_payload.json, the release manifest and onboarding.json follow; restore any .claude/skills churn regen makes before committing. Update existing tests in status_full/tests.rs that pin the old text. Sync the situation-layer concept (orient prints resolved paths and the next line, citing orient-host-playbook D1). One commit. Bee commands you may run: bee dev regen, bee dev release-manifest --check, bee onboard --repo-root . --json, bee orient --class bugfix, bee knowledge check. Run no dispatch verb, not even its help.

orient --class --json carries the same resolved paths as the text
